questions.question: For a full SVD of A with shape (3, 2), which shapes are valid for U, Sigma, and V^T?
questions.explanation: The full factors preserve the output and input bases: U is m by m, Sigma is m by n, and V^T is n by n.

questions.question: How can singular values be obtained from A^T A?
options: They are the eigenvalues of A added to its diagonal
They are the square roots of the nonnegative eigenvalues of A^T A
They are the row sums of A
They are the reciprocals of all entries in A^T A
questions.explanation: A^T A has eigenvalues sigma_i^2. Taking nonnegative square roots gives the singular values, ordered from largest to smallest.

questions.question: What does a rank-k truncated SVD keep for image compression?
options: The k smallest pixels in each row
Only the diagonal of the original image
The k largest singular values and their matching singular vectors
Every singular value, but no singular vector
questions.explanation: The leading singular triplets carry the greatest squared reconstruction energy. Dropping the rest gives the best rank-k approximation in the standard Frobenius norm.

questions.question: How does the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse solve an overdetermined least-squares problem?
options: It solves only if A is square and exactly invertible
It deletes the extra equations before solving
It chooses x=b regardless of A
It returns x=A+ b, the minimum-residual solution when the relevant rank conditions hold
questions.explanation: For a tall full-column-rank matrix, A+ b gives the least-squares minimizer. SVD handles rank deficiency by inverting only nonzero singular values.

questions.question: In A=U Sigma V^T, which factor acts first on an input vector?
options: V^T rotates it in the input space
U rotates it before any other factor
Sigma adds a constant bias
The factors act in the written left-to-right order
questions.explanation: Matrix multiplication applies the rightmost factor first: V^T changes coordinates, Sigma scales them, and U maps the result into output space.

questions.question: How is SVD connected to PCA after data is centered?
options: PCA uses only the left singular vectors of an uncentered data matrix
The right singular vectors are PCA directions, and squared singular values give variance up to scaling
PCA replaces all singular values with one
SVD and PCA cannot be related because one is supervised
questions.explanation: For centered data X, the covariance is proportional to X^T X. Its eigenvectors are the right singular vectors of X, with eigenvalues proportional to sigma_i^2.
